title: Before-count subtraction left an uncertain depth contrast for Mw 5.8 neighbors of GCMT earthquakes in 1982-2019
abstract: We tested a depth difference in nearby event counts around 1,286 Global CMT earthquakes with 6.5 <= Mw < 7.5 in 1982-2019. The primary neighbors had Mw at least 5.8 and lay within 200 km in three dimensions and 1 to below 30 days before or after each center. We standardized center magnitude across depth groups. The shallow-minus-intermediate difference was 0.531 neighbors per center after the origin and 0.450 before it. Subtraction left 0.081, with a 95% three-year block interval of -0.095 to 0.229. Surface distance gave 0.035, also uncertain. A planned Mw 5.5 neighbor check gave 0.390, with an interval of 0.214 to 0.563. The result therefore depends on the tested magnitude range. Centers can be parts of other sequences, so the before count is not a pure background estimate. This statistic does not identify causal aftershocks or overturn mainshock-specific depth studies. Sparse large neighbors, one retrospective catalog, geometry error, and limited dependence models constrain inference. The package preserves 15,280 event rows, 3,515 candidate pairs, all count and uncertainty evidence, source hashes, code, a figure, and repeat instructions.

display.caption: Before and after neighbor counts and all planned shallow-minus-intermediate excess-count checks. The main Mw 5.8 contrast is uncertain. The Mw 5.5 check gives a positive contrast. Intervals use three-year calendar blocks.
